newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: RESEARCH ALERT - Malaysia short-term rates seen up.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Malaysia short-term rates seen up.

text.p: Short-term interbank rates in Malaysia are expected to rise on Friday as banks will start taking positions ahead of a two billion ringgit bond issue, research firm I.D.E.A. said on Thursday.
"Despite the recent flush liquidity, interest rates in Malaysia are expected to trade higher tomorrow," it said in its research report.
Malaysian interest rates have been under pressure throughout the week due to liquidity caused by some central bank deposit maturities and inflow of overseas funds.
"After hovering around 6.30/50 percent last week, the overnight money in Malaysia has repeatedly tested BNM's (Bank Negara Malaysia) perceived floor of 6.0 percent over the last few days," it said.
The overnight rate on Thursday ended at 6.0 percent, once again as in the last few days, supported by large local and foreign banks who are also Bank Negara's principal dealers.
Bank Negara has announced an issue of a seven-year Malaysian Government Securities for two billion ringgit on September 30.
I.D.E.A. said its judgement was based on the rising swaps, particularly for one-week which have been bidded up to 5.30 on Thursday from 4.00/20 last week.

"This implies that while overnight money should move towards 6.50/70 percent, the one-week interbank rate should climb above the 6.50 percent support, towards 6.60/70 percent," the research firm said.
On Thursday, interbank rates were marginally higher for most tenors as demand for funds increased ahead of the issue.

Dealers said banks were covering more aggressively as outgo on account of the bond issue would be followed by payments for banks' fortnightly topping up of their reserve accounts with the central bank.
Banks have to maintain 13.5 percent of their deposits as reserves with the central bank.
"Most people are preparing for the bond issue. That is why there is some demand," said a local bank dealer.
One-week money was at 6.50/60 percent against 6.30/40, two-week at 6.80/90 against 6.70/80 and one-month was at 7.15/20 against 7.10/15.
Three-month money rose to 7.30/35 percent against 7.20/25 and six-month to 7.35/40 from 7.25/30.
